title: A local gardener’s business website
brief: A service-led site with real project proof and a reliable quote-request flow. Services, coverage and content require owner confirmation.
objective: A local visitor can tell whether the gardener serves their area, find evidence of relevant work, and request a useful quote from their phone.
success: The business owner confirms service coverage and every published claim and photo.
A visitor can reach the relevant service and request a quote without creating an account.
A real staging enquiry reaches the managed inbox, the owner can find it if email fails, and errors preserve the visitor’s input.

now: Home, service details, project case studies, coverage, about and quote/contact pages.
A short accessible enquiry form, phone links, image optimization and owner handover.
Accurate page metadata, sitemap, redirects and owner-approved privacy/legal content.
later: A CMS if the owner needs frequent self-editing; multilingual pages if actual demand exists.
Online booking only after service duration, travel and availability rules are defined.
out: Customer login, ecommerce, invented location pages or fabricated testimonials.
An AI chatbot, custom CRM, real-time calendar or complex animation system.

technologies.name: Astro + TypeScript + project CSS
technologies.role: Generate fast, content-led pages with a small amount of client code.
technologies.rationale: Most visitor tasks are reading, finding proof and sending an enquiry.
technologies.tradeoffs: An editorial workflow is needed for content changes; inspect any existing site before choosing a rebuild.
impacts: Generate fast, content-led pages with a small amount of client code.
checks: Core navigation, phone links and native form submission work without hydration.
Production build has correct canonical URLs, image dimensions and no broken internal links.
technologies.versionPlan: Pin compatible maintained versions after checking the implementation repository and deployment target; no version has been selected in this plan.
technologies.fitDetail: Works with the other components; it serves a distinct responsibility.

technologies.name: Netlify static hosting + Forms
technologies.role: Serve the site and collect enquiries in a managed inbox.
technologies.rationale: Combine deployment and form handling rather than build a separate application backend.
technologies.tradeoffs: Review form limits, spam handling, data location and cost before committing.
impacts: Serve the site and collect enquiries in a managed inbox.
checks: Form is detected in deployed HTML; a real staging submission appears in the inbox.
Owner can review spam, export and delete submissions; notification failure does not erase the saved enquiry.
technologies.versionPlan: Pin compatible maintained versions after checking the implementation repository and deployment target; no version has been selected in this plan.
technologies.fitDetail: Works with the other components; it serves a distinct responsibility.

technologies.name: Versioned content files
technologies.role: Keep services, coverage and approved project stories organized.
technologies.rationale: A small site can start with reviewed files and preview deployments.

alternatives: Add a CMS only if owner editing requirements justify it.
impacts: Keep services, coverage and approved project stories organized.
checks: Each case study has photo permission, truthful scope and owner approval.
A preview change can be reviewed and rolled back.

questions.question: Which jobs and areas should the site qualify?
questions.why: A useful enquiry needs a genuine match to the gardener’s services and travel area.
questions.recommendation: Get the exact list from the owner; do not make location pages from guesses.

options.label: A named service area
options.benefit: Clear coverage information and fewer unsuitable requests.
options.tradeoff: Need real boundary details and an out-of-area answer.

options.label: Case-by-case travel
options.benefit: Owner can consider larger jobs farther away.
options.tradeoff: The site must explain that eligibility is reviewed.

questions.question: Who will update services and project photos?
questions.why: This determines whether content files are enough or an editor is worth maintaining.
questions.recommendation: Start with reviewed content files if updates are occasional.

options.label: Developer-assisted updates
options.tradeoff: Owner depends on a maintainer for changes.

options.label: Owner-managed CMS
options.tradeoff: Needs roles, training, preview and additional integration checks.

questions.question: Should visitors request a quote or book a visit?
questions.why: Gardening jobs vary in scope, access, travel and seasonal availability.
questions.recommendation: Start with quote requests and let the owner arrange a visit.

options.label: Request a quote
options.benefit: Fits jobs that need a conversation first.

options.label: Book an assessment
options.tradeoff: Requires calendar ownership, buffers, cancellations and availability rules.

sections.title: How this site earns a useful enquiry

blocks.text: Working assumption: an independent gardener serving a defined local area, offering quote-based work. The real services, location, business name, photos and response times must come from the owner.

blocks.title: Content the owner needs to supply

cells: Service page
Offered work, exclusions, suitable jobs, quote factors, relevant photos.
Visitor can explain whether their job fits.
Project story
Permissioned before/after images, job scope and truthful result.
No stock photo is presented as completed work.
Coverage
Actual areas, travel rules and how out-of-area requests are handled.
No invented local-office or service-area claims.
About / contact
Business identity, contact details, real credentials and operating process.
Owner confirms accuracy and can receive enquiries.
Shared controls
Project button/input styles, native labels and error/focus states.
Components are reused across pages and work with keyboard/mobile.

sections.title: What happens after someone contacts the business

cells: Name
Required, reasonable length limit.
Owner knows who to contact.
Email
Required valid email.
A reliable reply address for the first version; phone remains an optional alternative channel.
Phone
Optional, allow international format.
Useful if the visitor prefers a call.
Service
Required selection from real services; include “Not sure”.
Direct the request without forcing an incorrect category.
Postcode / area
Required, do not request full address initially.
Check travel fit before collecting unnecessary details.
Job description
Required, bounded text; no attachment upload in v1.
Owner can decide what to ask next.
Preferred timing
Optional, no promise of availability.
Helps qualification without implying a booking.

items.label: Empty and invalid
items.detail: Associated labels, readable error summary, inline field errors and retained values.

items.label: Submitting
items.detail: Prevent accidental double click while preserving a usable recovery path.

items.label: Accepted
items.detail: Clear receipt and owner-approved expectation; no false booking confirmation.

items.label: Offline / provider rejection
items.detail: Keep input, explain retry and show phone contact.

items.label: Spam / missed email
items.detail: Owner can inspect the provider inbox and spam; staged checks include both notification and stored record.

sections.title: A small stack with a concrete delivery plan

blocks.text: No customer authentication, custom database, React app shell or booking engine is needed for the agreed enquiry-only scope. Owner access to the hosting/form provider is separate from visitor access.

blocks.title: What must be true at launch

cells: Enquiry
Submit on the real domain; find the saved request; receive notification; owner knows the follow-up process.
Accessibility
Keyboard-only completion, correct labels/error focus, contrast checks, touch targets and no page overflow.
Content
Owner verifies service coverage, claims, photo permissions, contact details and data-use information.
Search basics
Unique titles/descriptions, real business details, sitemap, correct canonical URLs and old-route redirects. No search-ranking promise.
Performance
Optimized images with dimensions, minimal scripts, mobile network checks and no layout shift from unloaded images.
Operations
Domain and provider ownership, backups/export, update responsibility and rollback to previous deployment.
